prompt.context: In the face of increasing healthcare costs and decreasing margins, our client, the board of trustees for St. Scorekeepers Hospital, is exploring whether a merger would combat market forces. Another local health system also located in Washtenaw county, Mount Ricks Hospital, is a potential target and our client would like to evaluate whether a merger would be beneficial to both parties to combat market forces.
prompt.question: What are your thoughts? Evaluate whether a merger between St. Scorekeepers Hospital and Mount Ricks Hospital would be beneficial to both parties.

clarifying_info.q: How many facilities do each hospital have?
clarifying_info.a: Both hospitals have 2 different hospital facilities, all of which are in Washtenaw county.

clarifying_info.q: What departments/service lines does each hospital have?
clarifying_info.a: St. Scorekeepers Hospital has: emergency, cardiology, OBGYN, and orthopedics. Mount Ricks Hospital has: emergency, radiology, dermatology, and oncology.

clarifying_info.q: How many patients did each hospital see last year?
clarifying_info.a: St. Scorekeepers (SK) saw 150,000 patients; Mount Ricks (RI) saw 200,000 patients.

clarifying_info.q: What is the average revenue per patient for each hospital?
clarifying_info.a: SK = $150 per patient; RI = $100 per patient.

clarifying_info.q: What are the variable cost rates?
clarifying_info.a: SK variable costs = 20% of average revenue per patient; RI variable costs = 15% of average revenue per patient.

clarifying_info.q: What are the fixed cost rates?
clarifying_info.a: SK fixed costs = 40% of average revenue per patient; RI fixed costs = 30% of average revenue per patient.

clarifying_info.q: What is overhead for each hospital?

exhibits.shows: A line chart showing revenue per patient trends from 1998 to 2018 for St. Scorekeepers Hospital, Mount Ricks Hospital, a Regional Competitor, and the National Trend.
exhibits.data: Y-axis: $50 to $300 in $50 increments; X-axis: 1998, 2003, 2008, 2013, 2018; four lines representing SK, RI, Regional Competitor, and National Trend.

exhibits.data: Legend: St. Scorekeepers Hospital (two locations), Mount Ricks Hospital (two locations), Competitor – BTB Health System; red shaded area = Washtenaw county.

exhibits.shows: A stacked bar chart showing the percentage breakdown of service lines for St. Scorekeepers Hospital and Mount Ricks Hospital.
exhibits.data: St. Scorekeepers: Emergency, Cardiology, OBGYN, Orthopedics; Mount Ricks: Emergency, Radiology, Dermatology, Oncology; Y-axis: 0% to 100%.

framework: 1. Understand current financial performance: Calculate NOI for each hospital (Revenue – Variable Costs – Fixed Costs – Overhead).
2. Assess merger rationale: Market forces (declining revenue/patient trends), strategic fit (service line complementarity), geographic overlap/consolidation opportunities.
3. Quantify synergies: Revenue synergies (cross-referral, broader service offering) and cost synergies (variable cost economies of scale, overhead consolidation).
4. Evaluate risks and feasibility: Regulatory approval, integration complexity, brand/culture risk.
5. Recommendation: Does the combined NOI after synergies justify the merger?

questions.prompt: Calculate the current Net Operating Income (NOI) for St. Scorekeepers Hospital.
questions.guidance: Candidate should build a simple income statement: Total Revenue minus Variable Costs, Fixed Costs, and Overhead. SK NOI = $4.5M.

math.setup: NOI = Total Revenue – Variable Costs – Fixed Costs – Overhead

questions.prompt: Calculate the current Net Operating Income (NOI) for Mount Ricks Hospital.
questions.guidance: Same structure as SK. RI NOI = $1.75M.

math.setup: NOI = Total Revenue – Variable Costs – Fixed Costs – Overhead

questions.prompt: What do the exhibits tell you about the merger opportunity?
questions.guidance: Exhibit 1: Revenue per patient has been declining regionally and nationally – no hospital is immune to market forces; supports merger rationale. Exhibit 2: Two of the four facilities are in close proximity, creating potential for overlapping patient populations and facility consolidation. Exhibit 3: Only Emergency overlaps; all other service lines are complementary, suggesting revenue upside from cross-referral after a merger.

questions.prompt: Brainstorm the cost structure of a hospital – what are fixed costs, variable costs, and overhead?
questions.guidance: See brainstorming section. Strong candidates will independently categorize costs into FCs, VCs, and Overhead without prompting.

questions.prompt: Calculate the post-merger NOI for the combined health system, applying the stated synergies.
questions.guidance: Apply three synergy levers: (1) Revenue +10% overall; (2) Variable costs reduced by 15%; (3) Overhead reduced by 30%. Fixed costs unchanged. Combined NOI should be $15.75M, representing $9.5M in cost/revenue synergy value vs. the $6.25M pre-merger combined NOI.

math.setup: Combined baseline then apply synergies: Revenue ×1.10; VC ×0.85; FC unchanged; Overhead ×0.70

brainstorming.prompt: What are the variable costs and fixed costs of a hospital?

recommendation: Recommend the merger between St. Scorekeepers Hospital and Mount Ricks Hospital. The combined health system would generate $15.75M in net operating income post-merger, representing $9.5M in synergy value versus the pre-merger combined NOI of $6.25M.

The complementary service lines (only Emergency overlaps) provide cross-referral revenue upside, and consolidating overhead and achieving variable cost economies of scale drive meaningful cost reductions.
risks: Regulatory roadblocks – merger may not receive regulatory approval (antitrust / certificate of need)
Logistical complexity of executing a complicated hospital system merger
Erosion of brand equity for one or both hospital brands
Potential culture clash between employees and clinicians of the two health systems
Analysis does not include transaction costs, which could reduce net value
next_steps: Announce merger and prepare for regulatory review
Reach out to insurance companies (payors) to negotiate better reimbursement rates
Develop a branding and marketing strategy to inform patients of the new enhanced combined health system
